Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — Aaron and I found the latency and cost controls compelling. Before we get to formal procurement, finance raised a couple of questions we need clarified around the proposed commercial structure:

- We are evaluating a 3-year commitment but would prefer an annual prepay for years 1–3 rather than a single upfront lump sum. Can you outline how Redwood models multi-year annual prepay discounts vs a single multi-year prepay?
- Our finance team typically needs Net 60 on larger vendor invoices. Is a Net 60 or Net 90 exception available if we align on a partial upfront schedule?
- If we do partial upfront, finance would prefer milestone-based payments (signing / go-live / post-pay). Is that acceptable from your side for revenue recognition and pricing?

Hi Sasha — great questions and thanks for the SOW. I've outlined practical options below, plus a term sheet attached for your procurement/finance team to review (Redwood_Pricing_Termsheet.xlsx).

Options (high level):
1) Annual prepay (preferred by many customers): you prepay each year for that 12-month period. Discount schedule we typically offer: 1-year annual prepay = 12% off list; 2nd consecutive prepay year = 15%; 3rd consecutive prepay year = 18%. This keeps you flexible year-by-year while giving progressive savings.

2) Multi-year single prepay (3-year lump sum): deeper up-front discount (example: 20% flat) in exchange for full prepayment and earlier revenue recognition on our side.

3) Hybrid: partial upfront + annual top-ups. Example milestone schedule: 25% at signing, 50% at go-live, remainder invoiced annually in advance. This allows finance to spread cashflow while still getting prepay discounts.

Payment-terms exceptions: by default Redwood’s standard is Net 30. For multi-year prepay deals we can be flexible if the payment structure is a partial upfront + milestone schedule: e.g., Net 60 on the remaining milestone invoices for invoices >$200k. Net 90 would require an underwriting conversation with our finance team (we can escalate).

Next steps I propose: 1) review attached term sheet and mark preferred option, 2) I’ll loop in our finance lead for a short call to confirm Net 60/90 feasibility and any vendor onboarding requirements, 3) Aditya can confirm technical milestones tied to go-live.

Cc'ing Aditya (technical) and Vivek (sales ops) to keep internal alignment.

Thanks,

—

Thanks Marissa / Sasha — quick note from finance:

- For any single-invoice amount > $250k we require Net 60 as a standard. We're willing to consider Net 90 only under rare cases and with CFO approval.
- If Redwood requires partial upfront to enable discounts, our procurement requires a milestone schedule for the remaining payments. Example we prefer: 25% at signing, 50% at go-live (defined as production rollout), 25% 6 months post go-live.
- Supplier onboarding needs: W-9, bank details, and a vendor questionnaire. Also ask your team to confirm revenue recognition language for prepay and any refund/reconciliation clauses if usage materially under-indexes.

If you can incorporate those milestones into the term sheet and mark which invoices would be Net 60, procurement can route this quickly. Priya from legal will redline the SOW once we have a term sheet.

Subject: Final proposal: CloudFin payment schedule and discounts (RF-2025-087)

Hi Sasha / Tom / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on our internal approvals, here is the agreed commercial proposal we can put into the SOW and DocuSign:

Summary (Option A: Hybrid annual prepay with milestone schedule)
- Term: 3 years (annual prepay option).
- Year 1 prepay discount: 14% off list (invoice for Year 1 due at signing for the 25% upfront portion + remaining prepay invoiced as annual prepay on Year 1 start date).
- Year 2 prepay discount: 16% if prepaid; Year 3: 18% if prepaid.
- Payment schedule (hybrid/milestone):
  * 25% due at signing (invoice 1)
  * 50% due at go-live (invoice 2) — go-live defined as production rollout with customer acceptance test sign-off (Aditya will confirm exact criteria in SOW)
  * Remaining 25% invoiced annually in advance for the next 12 months (invoice 3).
- Payment terms: Net 60 on milestone invoices >$200k. Redwood finance to accept Net 60 on these invoices for RF-2025-087; Net 90 requires CFO-level approval (please advise if you want us to escalate).
- Reconciliation: usage reconciliation at 12 months. If actual usage is <90% of committed prepay, a pro-rated credit will be issued for the overpayment (credit cannot exceed 12 months of invoiced prepay).

Alternative (Option B: 3-year lump prepay)
- Single prepay at signing for years 1–3: 21% flat discount. Standard Net 30 on refund/reconciliation credits (if any).

Next steps:
1) Priya — please review and we can incorporate language in SOW; I’ll send a DocuSign with the term sheet and SOW once legal agrees.
2) Tom — please confirm vendor onboarding checklist items (we will provide W-9 and bank details in the next 48 hrs).
3) Aditya — I’ve asked you to add acceptance criteria in the SOW; can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?
